issues.legal_issue: A plaint cannot be rejected at the threshold on the ground of res judicata when determining the bar requires examination of the pleadings, issues, and decision in a previous suit rather than the statements in the plaint alone.
material_facts: The defendant sought rejection of a plaint in a subsequent suit, arguing that a previous suit between the parties had already adjudicated the dispute over the property and sale.
The plaintiff's plaint disclosed that the previous suit was pending when the subsequent suit was filed and that the plaintiff knew of it.
The previous suit was decided after the subsequent suit had been instituted.

Determining whether the issues in the two suits were directly and substantially the same, and had been finally decided, required examination of the pleadings, issues, and judgment in the previous suit.
issues.conclusion: The plaint was not liable to be rejected on the ground of res judicata because that ground could not be determined from the plaint alone. The Court expressed no opinion on whether the subsequent suit was in fact barred, and permitted the defendant to raise maintainability before the trial court, which was to consider whether to frame a preliminary issue.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 7 Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, whether a suit appears barred by law must be determined from the plaint statements alone; the defendant's case and other material cannot be considered at that stage. Section 11 of the Code defines res judicata. Its application requires the previous suit to have been decided, the relevant issues to have been directly and substantially in issue in both suits, the parties to have litigated under the same title, and the issues to have been finally decided by a competent court. V. Rajeshwari v. T.C. Saravanabava, relying on Syed Mohd. Salie Labbai v. Mohd. Hanifa, Gurbux Singh v. Bhooralal, and Kali Krishna Tagore v. Secretary of State for India in Council, explains that the previous pleadings, issues, and judgment are ordinarily needed to establish res judicata. Kamala v. K.T. Eshwara Sa holds that a mixed question of law and fact requiring other evidence or the previous order cannot be decided under Order 7 Rule 11(d). Saleem Bhai v. State of Maharashtra, Church of Christ Charitable Trust & Educational Charitable Society v. Ponniamman Educational Trust, Raptakos Brett & Co. Ltd. v. Ganesh Property, Mayar (H.K.) Ltd. v. Vessel M.V. Fortune Express, and Shakti Bhog Food Industries Ltd. v. Central Bank of India reaffirm that the plaint alone is considered at this stage. Soumitra Kumar Sen v. Shyamal Kumar Sen likewise states that recourse to Order 7 Rule 11 is inappropriate where the res judicata contention depends on matters outside the plaint, while allowing maintainability issues to be taken up after issues are framed.

rule.if: threshold_plaint_rejection_application and res_judicata_is_ground and (plaint_alone_does_not_establish_prior_final_decision or deciding_bar_requires_prior_suit_record)

predicates.threshold_plaint_rejection_application: A defendant asked the court to reject a plaint before trial.
predicates.res_judicata_is_ground: The defendant argued that an earlier suit between parties litigating under the same title had already decided the dispute raised in the plaint.
predicates.plaint_alone_does_not_establish_prior_fi: The statements in the plaint alone do not establish that the relevant issues were finally decided in the earlier suit.
predicates.deciding_bar_requires_prior_suit_record: Determining whether the earlier suit finally decided the same issues requires examination of its pleadings, framed issues, or judgment.
predicates.plaint_not_rejected_on_res_judicata_grou: The plaint is not rejected at the threshold on the basis of res judicata.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks threshold rejection of a plaint for res judicata, and the plaint alone does not establish the prior final decision or deciding the bar requires the earlier suit's record, the plaint is not rejected on that ground.
